primary_root_cause: Damaged, corroded, or disconnected wheel speed sensor wiring/connector (open or shorted circuit)
other_likely_causes: Excessive air gap or debris/metal shavings between sensor and tone ring
Damaged or missing tone ring (reluctor) teeth
Corrosion or moisture intrusion at connector pins
Chafed harness from wheel/suspension movement causing intermittent short to ground or voltage
ABS module fault (less common than wiring/sensor issues)
recommended_first_check: Visually inspect and ohm-test the affected wheel speed sensor and its wiring harness/connector (front for C1032, rear for C1034) for continuity, correct resistance, corrosion, and physical damage, and check sensor air gap to the tone ring
reasoning: C1032/C1034 indicate the ABS module has detected an electrical fault (open or short) or a degraded signal in the wheel speed sensor circuit, which most commonly stems from wiring/connector damage or a failing sensor rather than the ABS module itself. Since ABS fully disables when this code sets, the bike loses anti-lock protection, making this a high-urgency safety issue that should be diagnosed before continued riding, especially in wet or low-traction conditions.
